summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded firmware experience in bare-metal C on STM32 Cortex-M4 microcontrollers, including timer-driven ADC sampling, interrupt-driven I2C sensor drivers, and FreeRTOS task scheduling with UART/SPI/I2C peripheral communication. Combines this systems level C/C++ background with applied AI/ML experience in PyTorch model training and fine-tuning, including a YOLOv8 object detection pipeline on NVIDIA Jetson that issues real time control commands to STM32 firmware over UART. Skilled at integrating AI/ML techniques into constrained embedded and real-time firmware pipelines.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Built PyTorch training pipelines using HuggingFace VisionEncoderDecoder API to fine-tune a document understanding transformer on a custom dataset.
Improved validation accuracy from 55% to 93% via improved preprocessing and model tuning.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) for Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver for real-time sensing and display.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping; implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ driving five servos.
Resolved 11 integration failures; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.
